name: Circuit de Monaco
layoutNote: Current Grand Prix layout (2015-present, Tabac re-profiled, 3.337 km); the 2010-2014 seasons used the 3.340 km version (3 m longer at Tabac).

findings.game: No tunnel: the 362 m stretch under the Fairmont hotel (game s 1514-1888) is open road under the sky; only its elevation is bridged (flat 7.6 -> 7.4 m).
findings.real: Covered from the Portier exit to the Nouvelle Chicane approach: OSM way 4230891 "Boulevard Louis II" tunnel=yes layer -1 (356 m) + way 1230247123 (6 m), portals [43.740362, 7.430326] -> [43.737778, 7.427973]; partly open to the sea on the left (Wikipedia: the tunnel is "a unique feature").
findings.proposedFix: Wire js/tunnels.js (already holds this stretch: from [43.740362, 7.430326] to [43.737778, 7.427973], open side +1) into main.js / audio (lighting + reverb), as planned for v6.2.
sources: OpenStreetMap (ODbL), Overpass API queries cached in devtests/track-audit/cache/overpass/ (fetched 2026-10-01): ways 4230891, 1230247123, 450334964 (footway in the tunnel)

findings.real: OSM (2026) maps the circuit through an 18 m covered section at the Portier roundabout (raceway way 1470365907 tunnel=yes layer -1, game s 1412-1430) with Boulevard du Larvotto passing over it on a bridge (way 92627405, crosses at game s 1406).
findings.proposedFix: Keep the "Portier underpass" entry of js/tunnels.js (from [43.741060, 7.429974] to [43.741084, 7.430250]).

findings.game: Generic 390 m lane beside the start straight: entry line at s 3202 (124 m before the line, after Anthony Noghes), exit at s 94; side right; 60 km/h.
findings.real: Right side and 60 km/h are correct (FIA 2026). Real lane (OSM way 850261588) leaves the track at s 2972, between La Rascasse and Anthony Noghes ([43.7323832, 7.4229757]), and the exit lane (way 1388331347) rejoins after Sainte Devote at s 268 ([43.7370216, 7.4221175]).
findings.proposedFix: Optional: trackData.pitEntry / pitExit points (new fields) so js/track.js can start the lane before Anthony Noghes and end it after Sainte Devote; until then keep side -1, 60 km/h.
sources: OpenStreetMap (ODbL), Overpass API queries cached in devtests/track-audit/cache/overpass/ (fetched 2026-10-01): ways 850261588, 1388331347

findings.game: Beau Rivage (Avenue d'Ostende) climb: max 9.2 % over 50 m, 9.0 % over 100 m (s 335-529).
findings.real: IGN lidar on the OSM line: 10.0 % over 50 m and 9.5 % over 100 m after cleaning, 11.5 % over 50 m raw; published "around 12%". The rest of the profile matches within 0.8 m (RMS 0.23 m), range 41.8 m (game 41.3, published 44).
findings.proposedFix: Optional: use the DTM median of 30 m instead of 50 m (DTM_MEDIAN_HALF 1 for mc-1929) to keep ~1 pp more of the Beau Rivage grade; no other elevation change needed.
sources: IGN RGE ALTI 1-5 m bare-earth DEM via https://data.geopf.fr/altimetrie (resource ign_rge_alti_wld), sampled every 5 m on the OSM centreline; cache devtests/track-audit/cache/ignalti/

findings.game: Curvature-derived banking 4-6 deg (inside low) at every slow corner: Sainte Devote 5.3, Mirabeau 5.8, Fairmont hairpin 5.95, Portier 5.7, Nouvelle Chicane 5.5, Rascasse 5.9, Anthony Noghes 5.5 deg (24 sections above 3 deg).
findings.real: No banking published for any Monaco corner (city streets with ordinary road crossfall).
findings.proposedFix: Cap the derived banking on street circuits (e.g. trackData.bankMax = 2 deg for mc-1929) or lower BANK_MAX globally; the hairpin would then also lose its 6 deg inward roll.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circuit_de_Monaco (wikitext fetched 2026-10-01: length 3.337 km; Avenue d'Ostende "maximum gradient ... around 12%"; Casino Square "44 m higher than the lowest part"; tunnel)

findings.game: Fairmont hairpin: centreline radius 9.6-9.8 m (12 m chord), half width 6.9 m, grade -5.8 %, bank -5.95 deg.
findings.real: OSM centreline radius 8.9 m at the same place; the data is correct. The "cannot take the hairpin at 20 km/h" complaint comes from js/car.js (minimum turning radius 10 m at 10 km/h).
findings.proposedFix: No track-data change; fix the steering lock law (v6.2). Lowering the derived 6 deg bank there (above) also helps.
sources: OpenStreetMap (ODbL), Overpass API queries cached in devtests/track-audit/cache/overpass/ (fetched 2026-10-01): relation 148194 ways 4230007 / 568187257

method: devtests/track-audit/west/: dump-game.js (game build), ovp.mjs / osm-fetch2.mjs (Overpass), osm-loop.mjs + pr-chicane-loop.mjs (OSM reference loops), layout.mjs, profile.mjs (DEM on the OSM line vs game), raw-vs-game.mjs, crossings.mjs, way-on-track.mjs, direction.mjs, corners.mjs, madring-bank.mjs; results in west/res/
globalNote: tools/build-tracks.mjs projects with kz = 110540 m/deg and kx = 111320 cos(lat) m/deg: at these latitudes north-south distances come out 0.31-0.39 % shorter than east-west ones before the official-length rescale (WGS84: 111044-111168 m/deg of latitude). Cosmetic (<= 4 m per km).
